passages.source_text: καὶ ὁ πατὴρ Ἥμαρτον, ἔφη, ὁμολογῶ. καὶ Ἀννουβίων Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐγώ, ἔφη, σὺν αὐτῷ δέομαί σου συγγνῶναι γέροντι εὐγενεῖ καὶ ἀγαθῷ ἠπατημένῳ· παίγνιον γὰρ γέγονεν ὁ δυστυχὴς τοῦ περιβοήτου. πλὴν ὡς γέγονε φράσω. ὁ ἀγαθὸς οὗτος γέρων ἦλθε προσαγορεύσων ἡμᾶς. ἐτυγχάνομεν δὲ αὐτῆς ὥρας κατὰ ταὐτὸν οἱ ἐκεῖ παρόντες ἀκούοντες Σίμωνος, ὃς ἀποδιδράσκειν ἤθελε αὐτῇ νυκτί, ἀκηκοὼς ἐπιδημήσειν ποθέν τινας ἐνταῦθα τῇ Λαοδικείᾳ ἐκ προσταγῆς βασιλικῆς ζητοῦντας αὐτόν. Φαύστῳ δὲ εἰσιόντι τὸν ἴδιον θυμὸν φήσας οὕτως πρὸς ἡμᾶς Ἁλῶν αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα συμμετασχεῖν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε, ἐγὼ δὲ μύρον τι σκευάσω, ἵνα δειπνήσας καὶ ἀναλαβὼν τὸ ἴδιον χρίσας πρόσωπον τὴν ἐμὴν πᾶσιν ἔχειν δόξῃ μορφήν. ὑμεῖς δὲ βοτάνης τινὸς χυλοῖς προεναλειψάμενοι ὑπ᾽ ἐμοῦ, οὐκ ἀπατηθήσεσθε ὑπὸ τῆς ξένης αὐτοῦ μορφῆς, πλὴν τοῖς ἄλλοις πᾶσιν ὁ Φαῦστος δόξει εἶναι Σίμων.

ἐκείνου δὲ ταῦτα προλέγοντος ἔφην Τί νῦν σοὶ ἐκ τῆς τοιαύτης μηχανῆς ἐστὶ κέρδος; καὶ ὁ Σίμων ἔφη Πρῶτον μὲν συλλαβόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἐμὲ ζητοῦντες παύσονται τῆς κατ᾽ ἐμοῦ ζητήσεως. εἰ δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ βασιλικῆς χειρὸς ἀναιρεθείη, μέγιστον πένθος ἕξουσιν οἱ τούτου παῖδες, οἵτινες ἐμὲ καταλιπόντες προσφυγόντ......... συνεργοῦσι. νῦν γὰρ σοί, ὦ Πέτρε, ὁμολογῶ τὰ ἀληθῆ ὅτι ἐφοβούμην τὸν .........στω τοῦτο μηνύειν. ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ καιρὸν ἡμῖν ὁ Σίμων ἐδίδου πρὸς τὸ ἰδιάζειν .......... μῶν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ Σίμωνος κακὴν ἐφάνη βουλήν. πλὴν ἐν μέσῃ γε νυκτὶ ἀναστὰς ὁ Σίμων τὴν ἐπὶ Ἰουδαίαν ἐποιεῖτο φυγήν, προπεμπόμενος ὑπό τε Ἀππίωνος καὶ Ἀθηνοδώρου. τότε ἐγὼ δυσαρέστως ἔχειν τὸ σῶμα ὑπεκρινάμην, ὅπως μείνας μετὰ τὸ ἐκείνους πορευθῆναι εὐθὺς αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὰ ἑαυτοῦ ἐπανελθεῖν ποιήσω, εἴ που δύναιτο παρ’ ὑμῖν κρυπτόμενος λανθάνειν, μήπως ὑπὸ τῶν Σίμωνος ζητούντων ὡς Σίμων ληφθεὶς ὑπὸ βασιλικῆς ὀργῆς ἀποθάνῃ. ἀωρίας οὖν αὐτὸν ἐξαπέστειλα πρὸς ὑμᾶς καὶ κηδόμενος αὐτοῦ νύχιος ἦλθον ὀψόμενός τε αὐτὸν καὶ τάχιον ἀπελευσόμενος, πρὶν τοὺς πέμψαντας ..................... ἐπανελθών. καὶ προσβλέψας ἡμῖν ἔφη Ἐγὼ Ἀννουβίων τὴν τοῦ πατρὸς ὑμῶν ἀληθῆ μορφὴν ὁρῶ ἐναλειψάμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος ὢν προδιηγησάμην, ἵνα τοῖς ἐμοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡ ἀληθὴς Φαύστου φαίνηται μορφή. ἐκπεπληγμένος οὖν σφόδρα θαυμάζω τὴν Σίμωνος μαγείαν ὅτι ἑστῶτες τὸν ὑμέτερον οὐ γνωρίζετε πατέρα. κλαιόντων δὲ τοῦ τε πατρὸς καὶ τῆς μητρὸς καὶ ἡμῶν αὐτῶν, ἐπὶ τῇ κοινῇ πάντων ἡμῶν συμφορᾷ συμπαθήσας καὶ ὁ Ἀννουβίων ἐδάκρυσε.

τότε καὶ ὁ Πέτρος τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς μορφῆς τὴν ἀποκατάστασιν ἡμῖν ἐπηγγείλατο εἰπὼν πρὸς αὐτὸν Ἤκουσας, ὦ Φαῦστε, τὰ καθ’ ἡμᾶς. ὅταν οὖν ἡμῖν χρήσιμος ἡ περικειμένη σοι πλάνος μορφὴ γένηται καὶ ὑπουργήσῃς ἡμῖν πρὸς ἃ κελεύομεν, τότε κἀγώ σοι τὴν ἀληθινήν σου μορφὴν ἀποδώσω πρότερον ποιήσαντι τὰ παρ’ ἐμοῦ σοι λεγόμενα. τοῦ δὲ πατρὸς εἰπόντος Πᾶν ὅ,τι ἂν μοι δυνατὸν ᾖ, προθυμότατον ποιήσω, μόνον τὴν ἐμὴν τοῖς ἐμοῖς ἀπόδος μορφήν: ὁ Πέτρος ἀπεκρίνατο Αὐτὸς ἰδίοις ὠσὶν ἀκήκοας τῶν προόδων μου ἀπὸ Ἀντιοχείας ἐληλυθότων καὶ εἰπόντων ὡς ἐκεῖ γεγονὼς ὁ Σίμων ἰσχυρῶς τοὺς ὄχλους κατ’ ἐμοῦ παρώξυνε, μάγον καὶ μιαιφόνον πλάνον τε καὶ γόητα ἀποκαλῶν ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον ὡς γλίχεσθαι πάντας τοὺς ἐκεῖ τῶν ἐμῶν ἀπογεύσασθαι σαρκῶν. ποιήσεις οὖν ὡς ἐγὼ λέγω, καταλιπὼν Κλήμεντα παρ’ ἐμοὶ καὶ προαγαγὼν ἡμᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν μετὰ τῆς συμβίου σου, ἔτι δὲ Φαυστίνου καὶ Φαυστινιανοῦ τῶν υἱῶν σου. συνέσονται δὲ σοὶ καὶ ἄλλοι τινές, οὓς ἐγὼ κρίνω δυνατοὺς ὑπουργῆσαι τῷ ἐμῷ θελήματι.

μετὰ τούτων ἐν τῇ Ἀντιοχείᾳ ....... ἐν ὅσῳ ὡς Σίμων φαίνῃ, δημοσίᾳ κήρυξον τὴν σεαυτοῦ μετα ........ Ἐγὼ Σίμων ταῦτα ὑμῖν κηρύσσω. ὁμολογῶ ἀδίκως καταψεύ ........ ἔστι πλάνος, οὐ μιαιφόνος, οὐ γόης οὐδὲ ὅσα ποτὲ φαῦλα περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγων ἔφθανον ὑπὸ θυμοῦ ἐλαυνόμενος. „δέομαι ὑμῶν“ αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ὁ τοῦ πρὸς ὑμᾶς μίσους αἴτιος αὐτῷ γεγονώς, παύσασθε μισοῦντες αὐτόν· τοῦ γὰρ ὑπὸ θεοῦ πρὸς σωτηρίαν κόσμου ἀπεσταλμένου ἀληθοῦς προφήτου ἀληθής ἐστιν ἀπόστολος. διὸ καὶ αὐτὸς συμβουλεύω αὐτῷ ὑμᾶς πείθεσθαι περὶ ὧν κηρύσσει, ἐπεὶ πᾶσα ὑμῶν ἡ πόλις ἄρδην ἀπολεῖται. δι’ ἣν δὲ αἰτίαν ὑμῖν ταῦτα ὡμολόγησα, εἰδέναι ὑμᾶς θέλω. ταύτης τῆς νυκτὸς ἄγγελοί με τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν ἀσεβῆ ὡς ἐχθρὸν ὄντα τῷ τῆς ἀληθείας κήρυκι δεινῶς ἐμαστίγουν. „παρακαλῶ οὖν“, μηδ’ ἂν αὐτὸς ἐγὼ ἄλλοτε ἐπελθὼν κατὰ Πέτρου ἐπιχειρῶν λέγω, μὴ ἀποδέξησθέ με. ἐξομολογοῦμαι γὰρ ὑμῖν Ἐγὼ μάγος, ἐγὼ πλάνος, ἐγὼ γόης. ἔξεστι γὰρ ἴσως μετανοίᾳ ἀπολῦσαι τὰ προπεπραγμένα μοι ἁμαρτήματα.

ταῦτα τοῦ Πέτρου ὑποτιθεμένου, Οἶδα, ἔφη ὁ πατήρ, ὅ,τι βούλει· διὸ μὴ κάμνε. ἐμοὶ γὰρ οὐχ ἧττον μελήσει ἐκεῖσε ἐλθόντι διαλεχθῆναι ἃ χρὴ περὶ σοῦ διαλέγεσθαι. καὶ ὁ Πέτρος πάλιν ὑπετίθετο Ὅταν οὖν νοήσῃς τὴν πόλιν μεταβαλομένην τοῦ μίσους, ἐπιθυμοῦσαν δὲ ἰδεῖν ἡμᾶς, πέμψας δήλωσόν μοι, καὶ αὐτόθι ἐπικαταληψόμεθά σε. γενόμενος δὲ ἐκεῖ αὐθήμερον τὴν ἀλλοτρίαν σου μορφὴν ἀπελάσας τὴν σὴν τοῖς σοῖς καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀπλανῶς φαίνεσθαι ποιήσω. ταῦτα εἰπὼν συνεῖναι αὐτῷ τοὺς υἱούς, ἀδελφοὺς δὲ ἐμούς, ἐποίησε καὶ Ματθιδίαν τὴν μητέρα ἡμῶν καὶ τῶν γνησιωτέρων τινὰς συναπέρχεσθαι ἐκέλευσεν. ἡ δὲ μήτηρ συναπελθεῖν αὐτῷ ὀκνηρῶς εἶδεν. Μοιχὰς γὰρ εἶναι δοκῶ τῇ Σίμωνος συνοῦσα μορφῇ. εἰ δ’ ἄρα συναπέρχεσθαι αὐτῷ ἀναγκασθήσομαι, ἀδύνατον ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτῆς κλίνης συγκατακλιθήσεσθαι. οὐκ οἶδα δέ, εἰ καὶ συναπελθεῖν αὐτῷ πεισθήσομαι. ὀκνοῦσαν δὲ αὐτὴν ἀπελθεῖν ὁ Ἀννουβίων προέτρεψεν αὐτὴν εἰπὼν Πείσθητι ἐμοί τε καὶ Πέτρῳ καὶ αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ φωνῇ ὅτι .... ἐστὶν ὁ σὸς σύμβιος, ὃν οὐκ ἔλαττόν σου ἀγαπῶ. καὶ αὐτὸς αὐτῷ συμ......... ταῦτα τοῦ Ἀννουβίωνος εἰπόντος ἡ μήτηρ συνελθεῖν ὑπέσχετο.

context.translation_policy_text:
# Translation Stance

This document states the translation commitments that guide every
decision in the People's Open Bible. Declaring them is an act of
honesty: critics can assess our output against our stated
commitments rather than guessing at hidden biases.

> **Status: first draft.** This document will be refined as the
> project matures. Input and disagreement are welcomed via GitHub
> issues.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Contested terms

The following terms appear frequently and carry heavy theological
weight. Our default rendering and rationale are recorded here.
Per-verse variance is documented in the individual YAML files.

| Greek / Hebrew | Default English | Alternatives considered | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| Χριστός *Christos* | Messiah where independently titular; Christ in the name forms "Jesus Christ" / "Christ Jesus" | Christ, Messiah | Preserves the title's Hebraic messianic meaning while using the recognizable conventional English personal name |
| κύριος *Kyrios* | Lord | LORD, Master | Matches covenantal and NT usage |
| δοῦλος *doulos* | servant | bondservant, slave | Uses reader-facing "servant" consistently; documents bonded-status and ownership nuance in notes/audit metadata |
| πίστις *pistis* | faith | faithfulness, trust | Main text: faith; footnote alternatives where contested |
| δικαιοσύνη *dikaiosynē* | righteousness | justice | Both renderings preserved in footnotes for Pauline passages |
| ἱλαστήριον *hilastērion* | atoning sacrifice | propitiation, mercy seat | Dynamic rendering for accessibility; alternatives footnoted |
| ἀγάπη *agapē* | love | charity (archaic) | Lexical cognates in source kept |
| σάρξ *sarx* | flesh (literal) / sinful nature (metaphorical) | — | Context-dependent; per-verse documented |
| μετανοέω / μετάνοια *metanoeō / metanoia* | reorient / reorientation; toward God where the context warrants making the destination explicit | repent / repentance (traditional); reconsider / change of mind in documented exceptions | See "Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)" below; do not homogenize regret, divine relenting, or distinct turning words |
| νήφω *nēphō* | clear-minded (most contexts); sober (where Paul explicitly runs the drunk/sober metaphor) | sober-minded | See revision notes in 1 Pet 5:8, 1 Thess 5:6 |
| יְהוָה YHWH | Yahweh | the LORD, Jehovah | Renders the divine name as a name. Where the NT quotes an OT YHWH passage using *Kyrios*, the NT verse retains "Lord" to preserve the Greek; the OT source verse uses "Yahweh". |
| אָדָם *adam* | man / humankind (context) | — | Context-dependent per usage |

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.

## Change log for this document

Material changes to this document are themselves commits. Prior
versions of the stance are preserved in git history.

- **2026-04-21:** Removed creedal affirmations (Apostles' Creed,
  Nicene Creed, Chalcedonian Definition) and replaced with a
  theological-stance section that declines specific creedal
  commitment. Translation philosophy and contested-terms table
  preserved unchanged; those are methodology, not creedal
  commitment, and the project actually runs on them. Added a
  "Translating into other languages" section stating POB's long-
  term intention to ship in every feasible major language, with
  the full revision pipeline and transparent supported-language
  disclosure. Per-verse YAML citing the old `doctrine_reference`
  values is preserved as historical record; those are not
  retroactively edited.
context.ambiguity_review_standard: Apply the supplied DOCTRINE.md ambiguity policy: a defensible contextual rendering may be used in the main text when material alternatives and the reason for the choice are preserved in notes. A unique or uncontested interpretation is not required. Distinguish (a) an unreadable or unverified source, omitted content, invented restoration, or a construction for which no defensible English can be given, from (b) ordinary lexical, attachment, or referent ambiguity faithfully preserved in English or explained with viable alternatives. The former blocks publication; the latter does not automatically block it. A note cannot excuse unsupported wording: the proposed main rendering must itself be defensible from the supplied Greek. Clearly printed gaps must remain gaps, not be filled by invention. Never change a verdict merely to achieve acceptance.
context.selected_edition_coverage_standard: Coverage is assessed against ALL SURVIVING WORDING AND PRINTED GAP MARKERS in the selected image-checked edition, not against unavailable words of a hypothetical complete original. A confirmed printed lacuna must remain an explicit gap in the English, retaining the exact number of printed dots (layout whitespace may differ), with a source-quoted note explaining that its content is unavailable and no restoration has been supplied. Such faithful representation can pass selected-edition coverage; it must never be described as recovery of the lost wording or an unbroken original. Distinguish this from missing scan pages, unverified ink, omitted surviving Greek, an unsupported English completion, or a translation that obscures the gap: those remain blocking. Neither this scope clarification nor a prior suggestion is an instruction to accept a draft; independently check every surviving clause, every gap, and every disclosure.

passages.text: And the father said, “I sinned; I confess it.” Annoubion said, “I too, together with him, ask you to forgive a noble and good old man who was deceived, for the unfortunate man has become the plaything of the notorious fellow. But I will tell you how it happened. This good old man came to greet us. At that very hour, all of us who were present there happened to be listening to Simon, who wanted to run away that night because he had heard that certain people were coming from somewhere, here to Laodicea, under a royal order to search for him. When Faustus came in, Simon stated his own intention and spoke to us as follows: ‘Halōn him when he comes, and make him partake with you. I will prepare an ointment so that, after he has dined, taken it, and anointed his own face, he may appear to everyone to have my form. But you will first be anointed by me with the juices of a certain plant, so you will not be deceived by his unfamiliar form; to everyone else, however, Faustus will appear to be Simon.’”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: παίγνιον γὰρ γέγονεν ὁ δυστυχὴς τοῦ περιβοήτου
lexical_decisions.chosen: the unfortunate man has become the plaything of the notorious fellow
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the image of Faustus as a plaything and the substantival force of περιβόητος without supplying Simon’s name.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἀκηκοὼς ἐπιδημήσειν ποθέν τινας ἐνταῦθα τῇ Λαοδικείᾳ
lexical_decisions.chosen: because he had heard that certain people were coming from somewhere, here to Laodicea
lexical_decisions.rationale: ποθέν means “from somewhere”; ἐνταῦθα and the dative name identify Laodicea as the destination or present location.

lexical_decisions.chosen: stated his own intention
lexical_decisions.rationale: θυμός can denote one’s inward purpose or disposition here; “anger” is possible lexically but does not fit the ensuing disclosure as well.

lexical_decisions.chosen: an ointment
lexical_decisions.rationale: μύρον denotes a perfumed oil or ointment; the following anointing favors “ointment.”

lexical_decisions.chosen: his unfamiliar form
lexical_decisions.rationale: ξένος here describes the form as foreign or unfamiliar to the observers, not necessarily as belonging to a literal stranger.

source_issues.source_quote: Ἁλῶν αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα συμμετασχεῖν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε
source_issues.issue: The printed Ἁλῶν does not yield a defensible construction with αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα and ποιήσατε. It has therefore been transliterated rather than silently replaced in the translation. The context appears to call for an instruction to take or secure Faustus when he arrives, but that sense is not supported by the printed form itself.
source_issues.proposed_reading: ἑλόντες αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα συμμετασχεῖν ὑμῖν ποιήσατε

passages.text:
While he was proposing these things, I said, “What benefit is there for you now in such a scheme?” Simon said, “First, those searching for me will arrest him and stop their search against me. And if he should even be killed by the royal hand, his children—who abandoned me, took refuge......... and are assisting—will experience the greatest grief.”

“For now, Peter, I confess the truth to you: I was afraid of the .........stō to disclose this. But Simon did not even give us time to confer privately..........mōn; to him Simon’s evil counsel appeared. Nevertheless, in the middle of the night Simon got up and fled toward Judea, escorted by both Appion and Athenodorus. I then pretended that my body was unwell so that, by remaining behind after they had gone, I might make him return at once to his own people, in case he could escape notice while hiding among you, lest he be seized as Simon by those searching for Simon and die under the royal wrath. I therefore sent him away to you at an untimely hour, and out of concern for him I came by night both to see him and to leave very quickly, before those who had sent....................., having returned.”

Then, looking at us, he said, “I, Annoubion, see your father’s true form, since I was anointed by Simon himself—ōn, as I related beforehand—so that the true form of Faustus might be visible to my eyes. Being utterly astounded, therefore, I marvel at Simon’s magic: although you are standing here, you do not recognize your own father.” As the father, the mother, and we ourselves wept over the misfortune common to us all, Annoubion also shared our grief and shed tears.

lexical_decisions.chosen: should even be killed by the royal hand
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the source’s personifying image of the royal hand rather than reducing it to an abstract governmental authority.

lexical_decisions.chosen: fled toward Judea
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπί with the accusative marks the direction of Simon’s flight.

lexical_decisions.chosen: return at once to his own people
lexical_decisions.rationale: The idiom may refer to one’s own home, affairs, or people; the following παρ’ ὑμῖν favors Faustus’s family or associates.

lexical_decisions.chosen: at an untimely hour
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive denotes action at an unusually late or otherwise inconvenient hour.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅτι ἑστῶτες τὸν ὑμέτερον οὐ γνωρίζετε πατέρα
lexical_decisions.chosen: although you are standing here, you do not recognize your own father
lexical_decisions.rationale: The participle ἑστῶτες is retained rather than omitted; the concessive relationship is supplied from context.

source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints nine dots after the surviving partial form προσφυγόντ. The unavailable wording and the completion of the participle have not been restored; the same nine-dot gap is retained in English.

The edition prints nine dots, but the surviving τὸν before the gap and final -στω after it do not form a defensible continuous construction. The ending suggests a dative such as Φαύστῳ, while τὸν is accusative. The translation preserves the mismatch and fragment rather than silently reading “to Faustus.”

source_issues.source_quote: ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ καιρὸν ἡμῖν ὁ Σίμων ἐδίδου πρὸς τὸ ἰδιάζειν .......... μῶν αὐτῷ τὴν ἐκ τοῦ Σίμωνος κακὴν ἐφάνη βουλήν
source_issues.issue: Ten printed dots interrupt the sentence and leave the fragment μῶν. Beyond the gap, the accusative phrase τὴν ... κακὴν ... βουλήν cannot straightforwardly serve as the subject of finite ἐφάνη. No defensible continuous English construction can be recovered from the supplied wording, so the fragments are represented without an invented restoration.

The selected edition prints twenty-one dots. The missing material prevents secure determination of how τοὺς πέμψαντας and the nominative participle ἐπανελθών were connected. The exact twenty-one-dot gap and the surviving syntactic fragment are retained without restoration.

source_issues.source_quote: ἐναλειψάμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος ὢν προδιηγησάμην
source_issues.issue: The nominative participle ὢν does not form a defensible construction with the first-person finite verb προδιηγησάμην in this clause. The context strongly suggests comparative ὡς, “as,” but the translation preserves the printed form as the transliterated fragment “ōn.”
source_issues.proposed_reading: ἐναλειψάμενος ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ τοῦ Σίμωνος, ὡς προδιηγησάμην

passages.text:
Then Peter promised us that our father’s form would be restored. He said to him, “You have heard, Faustus, about our circumstances. Therefore, when the deceptive form laid upon you becomes useful to us and you serve us in the matters we command, then I too will restore your true form to you, after you have first done what I tell you.”

The father said, “Anything that is possible for me I will do with the greatest eagerness; only restore my form to my own people.” Peter answered, “You yourself heard with your own ears from my advance messengers, who came from Antioch and said that Simon had been there and had vehemently incited the crowds against me, calling me a magician, a murderer, a deceiver, and a sorcerer—to such an extent that everyone there longs to taste my flesh. You will therefore do as I say: leave Clement with me and precede us to Antioch with your wife and also with your sons Faustinus and Faustinianus. Certain others will accompany you as well, whom I judge capable of serving my purpose.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: τῆς τοῦ πατρὸς μορφῆς τὴν ἀποκατάστασιν
lexical_decisions.chosen: that our father’s form would be restored
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀποκατάστασις denotes restoration to the former condition, here explicitly the father’s appearance.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the deceptive form laid upon you
lexical_decisions.rationale: περίκειμαι depicts the form as something placed around or upon Faustus; πλάνος characterizes it as deceptive.

lexical_decisions.chosen: my advance messengers
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantival plural refers to people sent ahead of Peter; “forerunners” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to taste my flesh
lexical_decisions.rationale: Preserves the violent bodily image and the source’s plural σάρκων without replacing it with a generalized desire to kill Peter.

lexical_decisions.chosen: precede us to Antioch
lexical_decisions.rationale: The following section shows Faustus going ahead and later notifying Peter. Formally, προάγω with an object can also mean “lead us onward,” but that is less consistent with the narrative sequence.

lexical_decisions.chosen: serving my purpose
lexical_decisions.rationale: θέλημα here is Peter’s intended plan or purpose, while ὑπουργέω denotes rendering practical assistance.

passages.text: “With these people, in Antioch....... while you appear as Simon, publicly proclaim your own change........: ‘I, Simon, proclaim these things to you. I confess that I unjustly spoke falsely........ He is not a deceiver, not a murderer, not a sorcerer, nor is he any of the vile things I formerly managed to say about him while driven by anger. I beg you—I myself became the cause of your hatred toward him—stop hating him. For he is a true apostle of the true prophet sent by God for the salvation of the world. Therefore I myself also advise you to obey him concerning what he proclaims, since your entire city will be utterly destroyed. I want you to know the reason why I have confessed these things to you. During this night, angels of God were severely scourging me, the impious man, because I was an enemy of the herald of truth. Therefore I urge you: even if I myself should come another time, attempt something against Peter, and speak, do not accept me. For I openly confess to you: I am a magician, I am a deceiver, I am a sorcerer. Perhaps it is possible through reorientation to put away the sins previously committed by me.’”

lexical_decisions.chosen: while you appear as Simon
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐν ὅσῳ gives the duration during which Faustus visibly bears Simon’s form.

lexical_decisions.chosen: not a murderer
lexical_decisions.rationale: μιαιφόνος literally evokes blood-pollution or bloodshed and here functions as an accusation of murderous violence.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ὅσα ποτὲ φαῦλα περὶ αὐτοῦ λέγων ἔφθανον
lexical_decisions.chosen: any of the vile things I formerly managed to say about him
lexical_decisions.rationale: φθάνω with the participle conveys having gone ahead or managed to do something; “formerly hastened to say” is also possible.

lexical_decisions.source_quote: ἄγγελοί με τοῦ θεοῦ τὸν ἀσεβῆ ... δεινῶς ἐμαστίγουν
lexical_decisions.chosen: angels of God were severely scourging me, the impious man
lexical_decisions.rationale: Retains both the appositional accusation τὸν ἀσεβῆ and the continuing force of the imperfect verb.

lexical_decisions.chosen: through reorientation
lexical_decisions.rationale: The term denotes moral redirection in this context; it is not rendered as mere regret or remorse.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to put away the sins previously committed by me
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἀπολύω can mean release, dismiss, or put away. The construction leaves some ambiguity between removal of the sins and release from them.

source_issues.source_quote: μετὰ τούτων ἐν τῇ Ἀντιοχείᾳ ....... ἐν ὅσῳ
source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints seven dots after Ἀντιοχείᾳ. The missing predicate or connective has not been restored, and the same seven-dot gap is retained in English.

source_issues.source_quote: δημοσίᾳ κήρυξον τὴν σεαυτοῦ μετα ........ Ἐγὼ Σίμων
source_issues.issue: The edition prints eight dots after μετα. Context suggests a word describing Simon’s change or reorientation, possibly μετάνοιαν, but the completion is unavailable and has not been supplied. The eight-dot gap remains explicit.

The edition prints eight dots after the incomplete verbal form καταψεύ. The object and completion of the verb are unavailable; the English preserves both the discernible accusation of speaking falsely and the exact gap without restoring the missing wording.

passages.text:
As Peter was giving these instructions, the father said, “I know what you want, so do not weary yourself. For when I get there, I will take no less care to say what ought to be said about you.” Peter again instructed him, “When you perceive that the city has changed from its hatred and desires to see us, send word and inform me, and we will catch up with you there. When I arrive there, on that very day I will drive away your alien form and make your own form appear unmistakably to your people and to everyone else.”

After saying this, he arranged for his sons, my brothers, to be with him, and he commanded our mother Mattidia and some of the more loyal people to go with him. But the mother looked reluctantly upon going with him. “For I appear to be an adulteress while consorting with Simon’s form. If I am indeed compelled to go with him, it is impossible for me to recline on the same couch with him. And I do not know whether I can be persuaded even to go with him.”

When she hesitated to leave, Annoubion encouraged her and said, “Believe me and Peter, and also the very voice, that .... is your husband, whom I love no less than you do. And I myself will be with him.........” When Annoubion had said this, the mother promised to go with him.

lexical_decisions.chosen: so do not weary yourself
lexical_decisions.rationale: κάμνω can mean grow weary or exert oneself laboriously; the father tells Peter that further explanation is unnecessary.

lexical_decisions.chosen: the city has changed from its hatred
lexical_decisions.rationale: The genitive τοῦ μίσους is taken as the state from which the city turns; “changed in its hatred” is grammatically possible but less suited to the following desire to see Peter.

lexical_decisions.chosen: we will catch up with you there
lexical_decisions.rationale: ἐπικαταλαμβάνω here denotes overtaking or joining Faustus after he has gone ahead.

lexical_decisions.chosen: appear unmistakably
lexical_decisions.rationale: The adverb means without deception or possibility of mistake, reversing the deceptive appearance imposed by Simon.

lexical_decisions.chosen: some of the more loyal people
lexical_decisions.rationale: The substantival comparative can describe more genuine, trustworthy, or devoted associates; “loyal” gives the contextual social sense without specifying an absent noun such as “disciples.”

lexical_decisions.source_quote: Μοιχὰς γὰρ εἶναι δοκῶ τῇ Σίμωνος συνοῦσα μορφῇ
lexical_decisions.chosen: For I appear to be an adulteress while consorting with Simon’s form
lexical_decisions.rationale: The mother speaks of how companionship with someone visibly bearing Simon’s form would make her appear; the translation retains μορφή rather than replacing it with Simon himself.

lexical_decisions.chosen: to recline on the same couch with him
lexical_decisions.rationale: κλίνη may be a couch or bed; “recline” preserves the literal posture while leaving the marital implication to context.

source_issues.source_quote: αὐτῇ δὲ τῇ φωνῇ ὅτι .... ἐστὶν ὁ σὸς σύμβιος
source_issues.issue: The selected edition prints four dots where the subject of ἐστίν would be expected. The context may suggest a demonstrative such as οὗτος, but no restoration has been supplied; the same four-dot gap is retained in English.

The edition preserves only the prefix συμ- before a nine-dot gap. It indicates association or accompaniment, but the particular verb is unavailable. The English gives only the general sense of being with him and retains the exact nine-dot gap.

## Theological stance

The People's Open Bible does not commit to a specific denominational
or creedal doctrinal stance. Where the source texts presuppose
theological claims — the divinity of Christ, the resurrection,
the personhood of the Holy Spirit, the unity of God — the
translation reflects those claims as the texts present them, not
as imposed commitments of the translator.

Readers from any tradition (Catholic, Eastern Orthodox, Protestant
of any stripe, non-denominational, inquirer) are invited to
evaluate POB against their own framework. Where a translation
decision is influenced by a theological reading — for example,
where a Greek construction is genuinely ambiguous and the English
choice leans one way or the other — that choice is documented in
the verse's `theological_decisions` block and the alternative
rendering is preserved in a footnote.

We do not pick sides on denominational distinctives (Reformed vs.
Arminian, infant vs. believer's baptism, real presence vs.
symbolic, cessationist vs. continuationist, etc.). Those questions
are for the reader and their faith community, not for the
translation.

## Translation philosophy

The People's Open Bible aims at **optimal equivalence**: the most faithful,
intelligible English representation of the source's meaning, wording patterns,
literary form, and rhetorical force. This is not an automatic midpoint between
formal and dynamic translation. Readability serves source fidelity; convention
and familiarity do not override it.

Specifically:

1. **Original-language primacy with reader-conscious wording.** Where
   long-standing English renderings obscure the source text's plain
   sense, we explain the source pressure openly. For *doulos*, the main
   text uses "servant" consistently while notes and the public audit
   trail preserve bonded-status, ownership, and total-allegiance nuance
   where it is historically or theologically salient (Rom 1:1, Phil 1:1).

2. **Translate titles; use conventional name forms.** Christological
   titles are translated to preserve meaning (*Christos* →
   "Messiah" when it functions independently as a title; *Kyrios* →
   "Lord"). In name-like constructions, use the familiar English forms
   "Jesus Christ" and "Christ Jesus." Personal names are otherwise
   transliterated by standard conventions. Thus "Jesus is the Messiah"
   retains the title, while Greek *Iēsous Christos* used as a personal-name
   construction is rendered "Jesus Christ."

3. **Preserve theological tension rather than resolve it.** Where
   the source is genuinely ambiguous on a contested interpretive
   question (e.g., *pistis Christou* — "faith in Christ" vs.
   "faithfulness of Christ"), we render one in the main text and
   preserve the alternative in a footnote, documenting the
   decision in the per-verse YAML.

4. **Consistency of key terms, or documented exception.** A given
   Greek or Hebrew word should receive a consistent English gloss
   across the translation, unless context demands variance — in
   which case the variance is documented per-verse with a
   rationale. The `consistency_lint.py` tool enforces this at
   commit time.

5. **Readable modern English, not archaic or academic.** The
   target reader is a literate 18–35-year-old English speaker.
   Vocabulary should be accessible without flattening theological
   weight. We avoid both ecclesiastical jargon ("propitiation" is
   footnoted, not required) and informality that undersells the
   text's gravity.

## Source distinctions and optimal English

Source fidelity takes priority over mere familiarity or defensibility. A
significant Greek or Hebrew wording pattern must receive an explicit comparison
with the best source-transparent English candidate, even when a prior draft
already discusses it in a footnote. Prior rationale is evidence, not a veto.
Do not infer different meanings from morphology alone or invent theology to
justify different glosses; preserve observable wording without adding claims.
A concise source-qualified or hyphenated rendering is available when ordinary
English otherwise conceals the source pattern. Record unresolved proposals for
maintainer review; do not silently certify them as unchanged or auto-publish.

**Approved scoped rendering:** John 21:15–17 uses **agape-love** for ἀγαπάω
and **phileo-love** for φιλέω, including the repeated question in verse 17.
The ἀγάπη noun's general table entry below is not a rule erasing that verb
pattern. Do not revert this approved POB/SPOB wording to generic “love”.

## Reorientation terminology (2026-10-11)

Maintainer-approved English POB and SPOB reader wording uses **reorient /
reorientation** in place of the repent family for moral-spiritual redirection.
Use **toward God** when the context warrants making that direction explicit;
use **toward you** in direct prayer, and omit the extra destination when the
sentence already names it, supplies a departure from wrongdoing, or concerns
interpersonal reconsideration. Acts 20:21 explicitly supplies the Godward
phrase. The word *metanoia* by itself does not lexically contain "God."

This is an English editorial policy, not a claim that remorse is irrelevant or
that Greek word parts establish the full meaning. Preserve sorrow, named sins,
faith, forgiveness, and the distinction between a response and its fruit.
Keep separate turning expressions in Acts 3:19 and 26:20. Baptism's relationship
to reorientation must not be rewritten as "only symbolizes" or "causes."

**Context controls exceptions.** Retain regret, relenting, reconsideration,
change of mind, or turning back where that is the supported sense. Do not make
God reorient toward God; do not make a persecutor's demand for apostasy a call
toward God. Preserve contested interpretations in Job 42:6 and Hebrews 12:17.
Extra-canonical authors retain their own conceptual frameworks. Adapting a
historical English witness is not a new ancient-language translation, and must
be disclosed while its source transcription remains untouched.

**No invented intensifiers.** Do not add "fully," "completely," "radically,"
"truly," "wholeheartedly," or a superlative simply to strengthen reorientation.
Preserve such force only where the source supplies it. Hermas V.3.xiii.4
(reader chapter 21:4) has *holotelōs* and *ex holēs kardias*; its existing
"completely" and "from their whole heart" are not new additions.

Traditional terminology remains in alternative notes, original sources, and
historical revision records. Do not rewrite those layers to manufacture a
history of agreement. See [the application report](docs/REORIENTATION_POLICY_2026-10-11.md)
and the hash-bound plan in `config/terminology/`.

## What the translation is not

To prevent misunderstanding:

- **Not a paraphrase.** Every English rendering is tied to a
  specific source-text word or phrase, documented in the per-verse
  YAML.
- **Not a study Bible.** Footnotes document translation decisions,
  not doctrinal application or devotional commentary.
- **Not a denominational product.** The translation is
  intentionally cross-denominational. Contested readings are
  preserved in footnotes, not smoothed away.
- **Not a finalized translation.** Every verse is currently an
  AI-drafted rendering, released openly with full rationale. There
  is no formal scholarly review process at this time.
- **Not a first-century English approximation.** We aim at modern
  English that honors source-language meaning, not at archaism.

## Translating into other languages

The People's Open Bible's long-term intention is to be translated
into every major world language. Scripture belongs to the whole
church; producing POB only in English would contradict the
project's mission.

Each target language is its own translation — drafted directly
from the original-language sources (Hebrew OT, Greek NT, Swete
LXX for the deuterocanonical books) rather than from the English
POB. Translating from English would compound the distance from the
originals and inherit choices that make sense in English but not
elsewhere. Every target language deserves its own encounter with
the Hebrew and Greek.

Each language goes through **several revision passes** before it
is considered stable:

1. **AI-drafted first pass** — a frontier multilingual model
   produces the initial verse-by-verse draft with full per-verse
   provenance, following the same methodology used for English
   (DOCTRINE.md translation philosophy §§1–5, per-verse YAML
   schema, `doctrine_reference` citations where relevant).
2. **AI-reviewer revision** — a second, distinct model reads the
   draft and flags awkward phrasing, dropped nuance, or places
   where the target language's idiom has drifted from the
   source's force. Revisions are discrete commits.
3. **Native-speaker community review** — before a language is
   declared stable, speakers of that language who are also
   familiar with the biblical source languages (or who have
   access to published lexicons in that language) audit the
   text and raise issues publicly.
4. **Public issue window** — a minimum public-review period with
   open GitHub issues before any language moves from "preview"
   to "stable."

**Supported languages will be disclosed publicly based on model
performance and feasibility.** Not every language has an AI model
capable of scholarly-accurate translation yet, and not every
language has a sufficient community of native-speaking reviewers
accessible to the project. We will publish the current supported-
language list, and the ready-but-not-yet-stable list, as we reach
the capability threshold for each. Languages that do not yet meet
the bar are named as such, not silently omitted.

Every language published under this program carries the same
CC-BY 4.0 license, the same per-verse provenance, the same
auditability. There is no tier system across languages — every
supported language gets the full People's Open Bible.
